A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same XTransfer work despite the revised title. Their complete text, figures, tables and Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix C report original classification, blood-pressure regression, ablation and edge-device measurements.

after.justification: Retains the original experiments and adds SemiCMT comparisons, alignment/PCA/backbone studies and training-time measurements.

M1.justification: The SRR connector, PCA alignment, anchor pairing, repair loss, channel removal and LWS procedures are retained. Expanded PCA explanations and experimental variants do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: The eight source datasets, seven target datasets, preliminary CUB reference and edge-device scenarios are retained. Added studies reuse existing coverage; additional backbones and PCA configurations do not introduce new tasks or populations.

E2.justification: SemiCMT is newly evaluated in the accuracy, ATR and GPU-utilization comparisons in Tables 4-6 and participates in the new training-time comparison. Existing comparator methods remain; changed citations for ProtoNet, MAML and loss baselines do not establish different methods.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds substantial controlled evaluation settings: alignment enabled/disabled across training epochs, standard versus sparse PCA, component-count alternatives, and a reported 5-shot comparison of three multi-source backbones. It also introduces a training-time comparison with defined timing scopes. Existing LOOCV and main 3/5/10-shot protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.1-C.3 and C.6 investigate alignment's contribution, PCA variant and dimensionality sensitivity, and backbone accuracy/resource tradeoffs. These substantially extend component validation beyond v1's existing repair-loss, removal, source-modality and search-depth analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: Both specify 15 rounds per setting, fixed random seeds and CUDA determinism, and retain the same graphical uncertainty reporting. The new tables introduce no additional confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Existing rows in Tables 4-6 and the on-device table are unchanged. V2 adds SemiCMT results and Tables 8-12 covering alignment, PCA, backbones and training time. For example, new 5-shot HHAR results give standard/sparse PCA accuracies of 71.85%/64.67%, while training times are 5.57 minutes for Our-Single, 4.62 for DAPN and 125.66 for MAML. These are added comparisons, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The alignment and repair-loss equations, resource-weighted search objective, repair-rate model and dynamic search-range expressions are retained. New qualitative PCA explanations introduce no formal derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Both already claim modality-agnostic, resource-efficient few-shot transfer through SRR and LWS, with strong sensing performance and reduced collection, training and deployment costs. The revised title and contribution wording preserve these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations concerning PCA orthogonality, backpropagation compatibility and backbone tradeoffs. Section 6.3 links low-shot instability to unrepresentative samples and source-target semantic relevance. The homogeneous-backbone restriction remains in Appendix C.6, alongside new assertions about heterogeneous and temporal-encoder extensions without corresponding tests.

D1.justification: Table 3 adds architectural, resource and input specifications for Multi-Conv4 and Multi-ResNet10; Appendix C.7 specifies which stages baseline training times include. Existing implementation and hardware disclosures remain. V2 also omits v1's explicit identification of the repair-loss distance as Euclidean without specifying a replacement.

R1.justification: Adds positioning against C3T, SemiCMT, IMU2CLIP and LLM-based sensor-data augmentation, emphasizing paired-data and semantic-alignment requirements. Several original method references, including those for ProtoNet, MAML, N-pair and triplet loss, are removed or replaced by benchmarking/sensing citations. The central novelty positioning remains.

P1.justification: Revises the title, author/affiliation information, opening narrative, contribution presentation and challenge/PCA explanations. Limitations are redistributed and citations switch to author-year style. The main section sequence and much of the method and experimental prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Adds five appendix tables, expands baseline/backbone and main comparison tables, and changes document typography, headers and table layout. The overview moves from Figure 3 to Figure 1 with revised labeling and an expanded caption. Existing empirical plots are retained, and the on-device table moves from Table 8 to Table 13.

improvement.justification: The added alignment/PCA controls strengthen previously incomplete justification of design choices, while SemiCMT and training-time comparisons make the empirical assessment more informative. These benefits support a modest net improvement. Some additions remain insufficiently reconciled: Appendix C.6 describes a 5-shot Multi-ResNet18 result of 78.44% in Table 11, whereas Table 4 reports 74.3%, without explaining the difference; broader compatibility assertions also lack direct tests.
